questions.answer: an unhygienic dorm (cockroaches, mould etc.) that we later found out was not earthquake-safe

questions.answer: a kitchen with some faults (broken oven, constantly dripping tap, mouldy airconditioner)

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: that if they still have not renovated/rebuilt the dorm, the health risks far outweigh the cheap price, so it would be advisable to find your own housing.

questions.answer: (in most cases)you show up to orientation and they hand you a folder of information and a list of class courses. You choose your classes, let the teacher know and they enroll you.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: the teachers were kind and helped students who were unsure decide the pros and cons of different classes

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: successful

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: you get a homeroom teacher that you can talk to about school-related concerns; things often get resolved faster when contacting them rather than the administration who might not know about the specific situation you might happen to be in at that time

questions.answer: BA

questions.answer: BA

questions.answer: the level felt relatively low academically (Danish high school level)

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
Host university: much passive listening, no breaks, simple expectations, lots of memorization for tests, the teacher encourages you to follow instructions 
UCPH: active participation, breaks, complex expectations, lots of writing, teacher encourages you to figure things out independently but with less clear instructions

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: While the overall cultural aspect of moving to a new country came with a lot of fun challenges, the social atmosphere at the school was really hard to adjust to.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The lack of academic motivation in students, which of course greatly depends on which school you attend (sleeping in class, not doing assigned work, talking over the teacher despite being shushed many times, ignoring the teacher even though they are being asked something directly, which all just contributes to a very specific class culture that can be hard to navigate as someone who likes studying/learning)

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: the availability. You can get a hold of almost any teacher at any time, should you have any questions

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. being left alone most of the time with little to no social events, you do actually get a lot of individual freedom. Learning to make the most of that is crucial.
2. only live in the dorm if they rebuild/renovate it. The health risks are not worth it. 
3. making friends outside campus (local cafes/volunteering/festivals etc.) can make all the difference, when it comes to feeling socially fulfilled, especially if you happen to be in your mid-20´s or above.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: there is a curfew at 11 pm

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: language progress

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: poor living conditions affecting our health (the mould in the air conditioners in the rooms causes similar symptoms to the flu) and not being able to do anything about it. In Japan you need a professional to come and clean out the inner parts of the air conditioner that cannot otherwise be reached, but every time we would ask for it to please be cleaned or for permission to call someone ourselves we were told no, since that would cost money.
